title: How Virat Kohli’s ‘Never Back Down’ Message Sparked PV Sindhu’s Return to Form
excerpt: India’s two-time Olympic badminton medalist credits the cricket legend’s guidance during her injury-plagued comeback, as she rebuilds her game with a new BWF leadership role.
body:
• PV Sindhu shared Virat Kohli’s private message — “Never back down, PV” — after the two met at the RCB Innovation Lab Indian Sports Summit in Bengaluru
  • The two-time Olympic medalist has been gradually rebuilding her form after a challenging year of injuries, reaching the Thailand Open quarterfinals
  • Sindhu has been appointed Chair of the BWF Athletes’ Commission, gaining voting rights on the Badminton World Federation Council
  • Her comeback mirrors Kohli’s own return from a nearly two-year century drought, which he overcame during the 2022 Asia Cup

When India’s greatest living badminton player needed guidance during the hardest stretch of her career, she turned to an unlikely mentor: a cricketer.

PV Sindhu, the two-time Olympic medalist and 2019 World Champion, revealed that a private message from Virat Kohli became a turning point in her injury-plagued comeback. The exchange came to light after the two sporting icons met at the RCB Innovation Lab Indian Sports Summit in Bengaluru, where Sindhu posted a heartfelt Instagram tribute to the former India cricket captain.

https://x.com/Inspirexo/status/2079264956328140919

“Every time I’ve needed guidance, you’ve always been there with the right advice and the right words,” Sindhu wrote. “There is no better example of what a true senior in Indian sport should be: generous, grounded, inspiring, and always willing to lift others up.”

Then she revealed the three words that mattered most: “‘Never back down, PV.’ Advice taken.”

The Comeback Trail

Sindhu’s road back has been grueling. A five-month layoff following an ankle injury, suffered during her victorious Commonwealth Games run, was followed by a season marked by seven first-round exits on the BWF tour. It was the kind of prolonged slump that can end careers.

Desperate to arrest the slide, Sindhu sought help from legendary Prakash Padukone and trained at his PPBA Academy in Bengaluru. She also drew inspiration from Kohli’s own well-documented struggle — nearly two years without a century — and his eventual comeback during the 2022 Asia Cup.

“Virat too went through a phase where he couldn’t score but came out of it. That is incredibly important, even for the best in the business and greatest athletes.”

— PV Sindhu

The results have been encouraging. Sindhu reached the quarterfinals of the Thailand Open before falling to Japan’s Akane Yamaguchi, and posted a third-place finish at the Malaysia Open in January. She also played a significant role in India’s Uber Cup campaign despite the team’s broader challenges.

A New Leadership Role

Off the court, Sindhu has assumed a position of institutional influence that few Indian athletes have held. She was recently appointed Chair of the BWF Athletes’ Commission, which grants her voting rights on the Badminton World Federation Council. The role gives her a direct say in the governance of her sport at the highest international level.

It’s a transition from competitor to statesperson — and one that aligns with a growing trend of Indian athletes taking leadership positions in global sporting bodies.

Kohli’s Broader Influence

For Kohli, the mentorship reflects a deliberate expansion of his influence beyond cricket. At the RCB Innovation Lab summit, he engaged in discussions on athlete performance, leadership, recovery, mental conditioning, and the future of Indian sports. The 37-year-old has been in commanding form himself in IPL 2026, sitting in the top 10 run-getters with 542 runs in 13 matches at a strike rate of 164.74, including a century and four fifties.

The cross-sport mentorship between India’s biggest names — cricket’s most intense competitor offering guidance to badminton’s most decorated champion — speaks to something larger about the Indian sporting ecosystem. As both athletes navigate the later chapters of their careers, their connection reminds a global diaspora that the lessons of resilience transcend any single playing field.
